title: On Running Project
subtitle: Premium scarcity strategy and AI transformation.
html:
View full presentation · Canva ↗

Aligning inventory with premium positioning

This project uses On Running as a case to connect pre-orders, inventory imbalance, wholesale distribution, and account communication. It proposes AI-enabled decisions and differentiated channel roles to address excess inventory and stockouts while protecting pricing, cash efficiency, and brand positioning.

The presentation starts from an approximately 70% pre-order model: early commitments can limit flexibility when demand changes. A mismatch between stock and demand can then create markdowns, longer inventory holding periods, and margin pressure.

Connecting market signals to inventory decisions

The first proposal combines social listening, search trends, sales acceleration, and regional signals to identify market opportunities and match them with overstocked SKU attributes. An AI decision layer would support targeted inventory releases, limited-release campaigns, and content development.

The aim is to connect products with suitable demand before resorting to broad markdowns, designing inventory actions and brand marketing together. This is a proposed workflow and technology concept rather than a completed system.

Assigning distinct roles to channels and AI

The channel strategy separates Growth Accounts, which support volume and cash stability, from Exposure Accounts, which support brand signaling, cultural influence, and scarcity. Their measures therefore differ across sell-through, order reliability, financial discipline, brand alignment, and influence.

A second AI proposal focuses on account management. Incoming messages and supporting data feed a decision process that routes work to automated responses or human review, reducing repetitive communication and preserving attention for judgment-intensive tasks.

Why the project matters

Inventory, marketing, and account management can work against each other when optimized separately. Clearance activity can weaken pricing, while an exposure-focused account may not be best judged by volume. The project connects these decisions and frames AI around intended improvements in cash cycles, cost to serve, and brand value.

This article describes a course analysis and conceptual proposals. AI workflows, channel changes, and expected financial benefits are not claimed as implemented company outcomes.
